topic: Neural Network Learning: The Intuitive Logic of Backpropagation
target_audience: University students with basic calculus and linear algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Learning Objective: The 'Black Box' Problem
sections.content: Establish the goal of a neural network: minimizing prediction error. Introduce the concept of a weight (w) as a 'knob' we turn to change the output.
sections.example: A robot trying to identify a cat vs. a dog. The initial output is random noise, and the goal is to shift the weights until the output matches the label.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Loss Surface
sections.content: Visualize the cost function as a 3D hilly landscape. The height represents the error. The goal is to reach the 'valley' (global minimum) using Gradient Descent.
sections.example: A hiker (the algorithm) descending a foggy mountain; they can only feel the slope under their feet to decide which way to step downward.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Backpropagation Mechanics
sections.content: Explain the chain rule visually. If the output is wrong, we trace backwards from the error, distributing the blame to each neuron based on how much it contributed to the final mistake.
sections.example: A chain of dominoes: if the last one doesn't fall, we look at the second-to-last, then the third, to identify exactly where the push was too weak.

sections.title: The 'Credit Assignment' Visualization
sections.content: Use a graphical representation showing the 'gradient' flowing backward. Thicker arrows signify higher contribution (greater impact on the error).
sections.example: A multi-layer factory conveyor belt: if the final product is defective, inspectors trace back through the stations to find which machine had the misaligned setting.

sections.title: Closing: The Iterative Loop
sections.content: Summarize the cycle: Forward Pass (Prediction) -> Loss Calculation -> Backward Pass (Update Weights). Emphasize that learning is simply repeating this until the error is minimized.
sections.example: A student learning to throw a ball: they throw (forward), see how far they missed the target (loss), adjust their arm angle (backpropagation), and repeat until they hit the bullseye.
